## By the Numbers

When Trump took office for his second term on January 20, 2025, 62 percent of white registered voters in Kentucky approved of Trump’s performance and 33 percent disapproved, according to Civiqs polling, for a net rating of plus 29 points for the president.

By September 24, 2026, approval had fallen to 43 percent, while disapproval stood at 46 percent, a massive 32-point plunge in net approval from the voting bloc.

Texas also began from a commanding position. [...] The figures come from Civiqs’ continuing online tracker of 132,219 responses taken between January 20, 2025, and September 24, 2026, so they measure changing opinion rather than polling on specific contests.

results.query: Civiqs "angry about the way things are going"

results.content:
Figures from Civiqs' rolling tracking poll of registered voters captured as of September 28 show the president is underwater in 39 states and every major battleground state.

Civiqs gives Trump a net approval rating in 10 states: Idaho, Wyoming, Utah, North Dakota, South Dakota, Kansas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Alabama and West Virginia.

Meanwhile, Civiqs puts the president’s overall approval rating at 34 percent.
results.title: Trump’s Approval Rating Hits Record Low Across Both Terms As Midterms Near - Newsweek

results.content:
Polling from Civiqs’ rolling tracker shows that in Alabama, Trump maintains a net approval rating of +5, which stands in contrast to most other states where he has a net negative rating as the Iran war rages and Americans grapple with high prices.

Alabama Republican candidates are also choosing to attend his rally, which isn’t necessarily the case in battleground states this cycle, where GOP candidates could view the president as a liability rather than an asset.
results.title: Why Trump's Mobile rally is about image rather than vulnerability in Alabama - Alabama Daily News
